slides.title: Second and third conditionals
slides.subtitle: Imaginary present and past
goals: Talk about **unreal past** situations and regrets (3rd).
Use **If I were you** for advice.

slides.title: Two unreal conditionals

head: Type
Form
Example
rows: If I **had** more time, I**'d learn** Japanese.
If + past perfect, would have + participle
If I **had studied**, I **would have passed**.

slides.tip: *If I were you, I'd…* is the standard way to give advice. Use **were** for all persons in formal English.

items.en: If I won the lottery, I would travel the world.
What would you do if you saw a ghost?
If we had left earlier, we wouldn't have missed the bus.
She would have come if you had invited her.

items.q: If I ___ rich, I'd buy a house.
If you had told me, I ___ you.
If I were you, I ___ apologize.

items.t: If it ___ (not / rain) yesterday, we would have gone out.
What ___ you do if you lost your phone?
If I knew the answer, I ___ tell you.
